Browser settings

Checkpoint saves and snapshot evaluation

Every manual save and autosave first retains the exact checkpoint snapshot and requests its browser download, then evaluates that same snapshot.

Autosave uses absolute cumulative committed prediction targets, not updates multiplied by a window size. Fresh-session default 5 million. Fractional millions are accepted; clear the value or enter 0 for Off. Successful saves continue training automatically. Optional Test on autosave measures the saved snapshot first; it is off by default. Required paired/strict safety and final evaluation remain unchanged; failures pause training. Saves finish the committed update crossing a threshold, so counts may overshoot. Paused edits switch to target units and start at the next absolute interval after current progress. Legacy checkpoints retain explicitly labeled update cadence until edited. Evaluation uses the selected held-out token cap and policy. No optimizer update runs during evaluation. Checkpoint and evaluation time are excluded from active training speed and training ETA.

Autosave: every 5 million committed prediction targets. Training continues after successful checkpoint work; Test on autosave is off by default.

A browser download request does not verify a disk save. Check the downloaded file before closing this tab.

After recovery: pending exact-snapshot evaluation.

“After recovery” shows only a completed evaluation bound to the exact saved snapshot. It is not the score of later training updates or an unfinished evaluation.

Training budget and measurement limits

Completing the selected training budget is different from covering the full corpus. A checkpoint saved partway through that budget is partial training, even when its evaluation completes. Completed evaluation means the selected evaluation budget finished, not that the entire held-out split was measured.

These controls do not measure watts, regulate power or temperature, or guarantee hardware or electrical safety.

Recent snapshot evaluations and save requests

The latest 32 entries are retained in each history. Autosaves use unique filenames. Browsers may ask you to allow multiple downloads. History field names remain machine-readable and are not translated.

Corpus Test A · recovery with live training ETA
Training completion prepares a checkpoint and requests its download first, then tests the final in-memory weights. Retry after evaluation without repeating training.


Open this file in a separate tab after saving your current run. It cannot read another tab's training state. A requested browser download is not confirmation that a file was saved to disk. Verify your checkpoint download before closing this tab. This trains LittleBit factor masters and exports a packed GGUF; it does not train a LoRA adapter.


What & why: Experiment label
A descriptive name saved with checkpoints and reports. Use Corpus Test A or Corpus Test B to keep results separate. It does not change training math, settings identity, or the evaluation benchmark.
What & why: Training preset
General recovery trains the compressed student against the matching Q8 teacher. Assistant-only SFT trains only answer targets in independent complete conversations. Choose the objective you intend; the losses and perplexities are not interchangeable.


1 · Choose the recovery preset


Both the original general-recovery corpus and verified Nexus job corpus are included. General recovery requires the original Q8 teacher; job SFT uses it only for optional comparison. For full broad-corpus teacher/student recovery, import the .nxcorpus file; it selects General five-stage recovery and a complete one-pass training budget. The original Q8 teacher is required. Its five contiguous training spans are consumed once without replay. A smaller budget uses prefixes of all five spans. For assistant-only SFT, import one ZIP in the same export format, or select train.unique.encoded.jsonl, development.encoded.jsonl and probe.encoded.jsonl together. Optionally include train.sequence_index.jsonl to reproduce a repeated schedule. Raw text and messages JSONL are not silently retokenized.


What & why: Encoded training corpus
Load an already-tokenized .nxcorpus or supported SFT archive/files. Import validates identity and split isolation before replacing the corpus. Broad-corpus import sets a full-pass budget; import the matching exposure plan afterward to select its exact schedule. Import can use substantial host RAM.


What & why: Explicit exposure plan
Load a matching immutable-record schedule after the corpus. It fixes exact target budget and context and checks corpus, tokenizer, ledger and plan hashes. Corpus Test A uses the sealed 20M plan with context 256. A different plan cannot exact-resume this run.
This separate candidate supports immutable-record schedules with exact target budgets. A plan can revisit selected records without copying them into the corpus. It uses independent record-local windows. The original five-span mode remains available without a plan. CPU/control-flow validation only; full-model GPU quality and throughput remain unverified.
Large corpus import uses host RAM, separately from the GPU allocation ceiling below. Progress includes a RAM estimate. Keep the tab open and use Cancel corpus import if necessary. A cancelled or failed import keeps the previous corpus.

2 · Load the saved model


What & why: Original Q8 teacher
Select the original matching Q8 GGUF. General recovery requires it for distillation; job SFT uses it only for an optional held-out comparison. Model architecture and tokenizer must match the student.


What & why: Compressed student
Select the original packed LittleBit factor GGUF. Training updates its FP32 factor masters; exports create a new packed model. A checkpoint must match this original file identity, not a different exported student.


What & why: Checkpoint mode
New starts from the selected student. Exact resume restores recorded progress, optimizer and scores with matching settings. Another cycle resets progress and optimizer. Weights-only warm-start copies factors but starts a fresh training/evaluation cycle. Choose explicitly; a checkpoint file alone does not select a safe mode.


What & why: Saved checkpoint
Select a .nqat file only with Exact resume, Another cycle or Weights-only warm-start. Keep the original checkpoint unchanged. Exact resume requires the same model, corpus, plan and settings; warm-start deliberately discards optimizer/progress/metric state.


What & why: Training target budget
Millions of committed training exposures: general recovery counts prediction targets; SFT counts whole-record input exposures and separately reports answer targets. Default 20M for Corpus Test A. A loaded exposure plan supplies its exact budget. Imported no-plan recovery cannot exceed one full pass.


Advanced training settings


What & why: Sequence length / context
Maximum prediction positions per independent general-recovery window. New-run choices100–1000 in100-token increments, default700; saved plans and checkpoints retain their exact read-only length, including legacy512/1024/2048. No rounding is performed. Larger context can improve usable context but changes the training trajectory and raises GPU memory needs; 256-token FP32 logits alone require 48 MiB. Supported experimental general range 8–2048; above 512 requires per-context device qualification and all contexts above 256 require graph allocation preflight. 512-token FP32 logits alone require 96 MiB. At 512, the selected profile uses its qualified shared-list kernel or the ordered scalar fallback. Exact resume and explicit plans lock this value; SFT always keeps full records.



Experimental strong-first → normal recovery (default on)


Two-phase LR controls and safety limits






Schedule, safety gates and evidence
The base LR below keeps the existing 2% warmup and cosine decay. Phase 1 multiplies that LR by 2 by default, until the first completed update crossing 10% of the selected training-target budget; phase 2 uses the ordinary 1× schedule. These are two phases inside one budget, not two complete corpus passes. Source-record order is unchanged and the boundary may overshoot by one update.


Default-on is an experimental conservative choice, not a proven optimal setting. Small toy recovery tests suggested some strong-first benefit; a limited actual SmolLM2-135M dense CPU test was worse at 10× and 100×. Neither establishes full-model LittleBit/WebGPU quality. The multiplier is limited to 1–4×, and base LR × multiplier cannot exceed 0.001.


Before the first optimizer update, the app retains a CPU-side snapshot of all factor masters, Adam moments and counters. The same held-out slice is checked after the first update and at the phase boundary (default 512 targets, at most the evaluation cap). A rise beyond 5% PPL, or a nonfinite result, restores the full snapshot and pauses. Continue then starts the ordinary schedule from that snapshot. Discarded attempts are reported and only consume extra compute if you continue; the committed target budget never doubles. Snapshot bytes increase browser RAM and strong-phase checkpoint size. Failed or cancelled evaluation pauses safely for a retry. Device/write failures require the saved checkpoint if automatic rollback cannot be verified.


Exact resume restores the saved phase, LR settings, target cursor, gates and snapshot. Older checkpoints keep their original single-phase behavior. New, warm-start and another-cycle general recovery use this default. Job SFT keeps its original schedule. Gates are development-set checks, not final quality guarantees.




Corpus analyzer & new/replay pass planner


Choose a supported ledger-aware .nxcorpus above. This editor keeps the source file and held-out splits intact, then creates a separate executable exposure-plan JSON. Encoded Job SFT JSONL/ZIP keeps its existing import path. Raw TXT, ordinary JSONL, and corpora for other tokenizers are not silently converted or relabeled.




Load a ledger-aware general-recovery corpus to inspect unique records and held-out boundaries.

New/replay pass settings










Each pass has a requested prediction-target budget and a new-data percentage. New records come first; replay follows and may only use records from earlier passes. A whole source record is indivisible, so the realized budget can differ. The preview gives exact executed counts. “New” is relative to this plan, not the model’s unknown earlier training.






No generated plan. Previewing or exporting a plan does not start training.


Requested versus realized passes and ordered preview
No preview.


Applying sets the exact realized target budget and context used by the existing record-local scheduler. Exact resume requires this same corpus and exported plan. Save both files. Clearing the plan restores the original five-span sampler. The opening LR phases remain a separate setting and do not add passes.




What & why: Learning rate
Peak Adam learning rate with the existing warmup/cosine schedule. Default 0.00003 from the verified screenshots. Larger values may adapt faster but risk instability or forgetting. It must be greater than zero and at most 0.001; exact resume requires the recorded value.


What & why: Training allocation ceiling
Upper bound for all tracked training allocations, including temporary cache, in MiB. Experimental default: user-selected RX 7900 XTX profile and 22,500 MiB. RX 7900 XT caps at 16,000; Manual caps at 24,000. This is not detected VRAM or reserved memory. Actual device binding limits and graph reserve can reject a run; other applications and the driver also consume memory.


What & why: Automatic before/after cap
Maximum held-out input/prediction positions for each automatic score. Default 32,768 from the screenshots; allowed range 8–32,768. More held-out targets reduce sampling noise but increase evaluation time. Keep the exact same benchmark, cap and context for a fair comparison. SFT must fit complete records.
Training masters and optimizer state use more memory than the packed model. Full job records may need substantially more memory than length 32; records are never shortened or skipped to fit. Stop and save a checkpoint during long runs. Full-model quality, GPU fit and throughput remain unverified. The one-update option still performs the configured development checks before training. Job SFT uses one fixed whole-record pass; use another cycle for another pass.


3 · Perplexity results (lower is better)
Metric details


Shared held-out benchmark for Test A / Test B
Choose the training corpus first. Export one verified development benchmark, then import the identical file into both tests before loading the run. Each import rejects source token/content/family/component overlap with that training corpus. This does not prove absence of semantic paraphrases. Loading another corpus clears the benchmark. Fresh Q8, before and after scores use exactly the same tokens, record boundaries, context and full-vocabulary loss. Earlier scores such as 167.19 use a different evaluation contract and are historical only.
What & why: Shared frozen held-out benchmark
Import the exact same exported benchmark JSON for Corpus Test A and Corpus Test B after choosing the training corpus and before loading a run. It freezes held-out tokens, record boundaries and tokenizer identity. Import checks token/content/family/component overlap against training data; it cannot prove no semantic paraphrases. Maximum file size 24 MiB. General recovery only.
Audited evaluation reads FP32 logits and computes stable Float64 full-vocabulary NLL on the CPU. It can take longer than the former GPU-only reduction; training kernels and update rate are unchanged. Every new metric has exact total NLL, target count, context, masks, corpus/tokenizer/model identities and a completion receipt.
4 · Evaluate without an update


Use development while tuning. Reserve final probes for your chosen model. Imported general-recovery streams evaluate every prediction position in the selected held-out stream; SFT evaluates complete held-out conversations. The bundled general corpus has no separate probe stream. Evaluation never contributes training gradients, changes the optimizer, or advances training counters.


What & why: Manual evaluation split
Development is for tuning; final probes are for the chosen model. Manual evaluation is read-only and covers the selected complete held-out set. Repeatedly tuning on probes weakens their value as an independent test.


What & why: Final-probe confirmation
Confirm you have selected the model before testing final probes. Inspecting them repeatedly while tuning can leak test information into model choices.


Separate evaluation report
No manual evaluation has run.


Throughput and stability


What & why: Execution profile
Default Throughput uses the previously shown bounded buffer reuse, coalesced scalar readbacks and grouped passes. It may be slower on a particular GPU; compare measured committed-target rates and keep Baseline available. Experimental GEMM/embedding profiles require their disposable parity check. Execution profiles do not intentionally change FP32 objectives, optimizer updates, corpus order or context.
These WebGPU presets change only the embedding-gradient kernel workgroup size and column stride. They do not change GEMM, GPU clock, PyTorch execution or promise a speed multiplier. Pause, select a preset, then Continue to qualify and apply it. Compare actual committed-target rates.


What & why: Temporary buffer-cache ceiling
Limit reusable temporary buffers within the total allocation ceiling. GPU setup uses the measured 128 MiB cache starting point; 256, 512, 1024 and 2048 MiB remain available. Stored preferences and exact checkpoint allocation are retained. This is an opportunistic cache cap, not an upfront reservation. A larger cache does not guarantee faster training and cannot bypass the overall allocation ceiling.
Requires validated live GPU telemetry and a safe-boundary transition. No automatic switching in this build.
Window control doubles input tokens per optimizer update, up to 2048. It changes causal context and the training trajectory; it is not independent minibatching. Available only before loading a new or weights-only warm-start run. Exact resume keeps its recorded window. Cache changes cannot exceed the total allocation ceiling.
No completed training updates measured yet.


On by default; uncheck to use individual uploads. Uploads each packed page before its existing submission; no additional GPU waits. Aligned page padding counts against the unchanged allocation ceiling and cache cap. Independent device qualification required before loading. Radeon speed benefit is unmeasured.
Off by default; requires a pooled profile. Keeps the existing cache ceiling (default 128 MiB), with no additional reserve. Qualifies on disposable tensors before loading. Intended to reduce buffer-object churn, not memory bandwidth or guaranteed speed.
Off by default. Qualifies on disposable tensors before loading. Same numerical checks, buffers and waits; fewer submissions are not a guaranteed speed gain. Enable phase timings for a measured A/B trace.
Scheduling diagnostics (optional)
Phase profiling off.
Enable while paused, then run a representative interval and export. No extra GPU synchronization is added. Wait durations include queued GPU work and browser/driver scheduling; they do not measure GPU idle time. Bounded to128 recent updates. Timings add small CPU overhead; no speedup is promised.


Throughput is the default from your verified screenshots. It is not guaranteed faster; Baseline remains selectable for comparison. Diagnostic profiles isolate one execution change at a time; none guarantees 150 tokens/s. FP32 math, sequence length, optimizer updates and corpus order stay unchanged. Live training-target rate is time-weighted over the last 10 active seconds and the text monitor refreshes about every 350 ms when the browser event loop permits; the current-session average excludes pauses, setup and evaluation. Local start/end times include the time zone; exports use UTC. Checkpoint history is not assigned invented elapsed time; up to 4,096 updates are retained. GPU temperature, power, utilization, clocks and total VRAM are not exposed here: use AMD Adrenalin Performance → Metrics → Start Logging and align its timestamps with the exported UTC timeline. A slowdown is not proof of thermal throttling. Keep the original run/checkpoint until local A/B verification passes.


Button help and safety notes
Bundled preset corpus
Restore the original embedded corpus for the chosen preset after saving/resetting a loaded run. This changes training and, unless a separate benchmark is selected, held-out data. Import the intended comparison corpus explicitly for a controlled test.
Clear exposure plan
Return imported general recovery to the original five-contiguous-span sampler. This changes the training order and boundary behavior; it is allowed only before loading a run. Save/reset first.
Cancel import
Stop a pending corpus import. The previous validated corpus is kept if import is cancelled or fails.
Full imported budget
Select the imported corpus’s full one-pass budget. With an explicit exposure plan, its exact target budget controls the run. A smaller arbitrary budget must not silently truncate an immutable plan.
Export shared benchmark
Export the selected general corpus’s verified development records as one frozen benchmark before loading a model. Import this identical file into both study arms. A shared benchmark makes scores comparable only when context, target cap, model start and evaluation policy also match.
Use corpus held-out data
Remove the shared benchmark before loading a run. Automatic evaluation will use the selected corpus’s own held-out records. Scores from different held-out sets are not directly comparable. Loading another training corpus also clears the benchmark and requires revalidation.
Evaluate selected set
Measure the current model without an optimizer update. This does not advance training counters or replace the automatic before/after pair. A loaded usable model and valid held-out set are required.
Double input window
Explicitly double the general-recovery input window, up to 2048, only before a new or weights-only warm-start run. It changes context and the training trajectory rather than independent minibatch size. Applied plans remain locked; build a separate plan for the selected context.
Profile parity check
Run disposable tensor tests before loading a recovery model. This checks selected kernel outputs/gradients/optimizer behavior on this device, not full-model training quality or sustained GPU speed.
Throughput CSV
Download up to 4,096 measured update rows with UTC timestamps, committed target counts and rates. No GPU sensors are inferred; combine with external GPU metrics if needed.
Stability report
Download bounded telemetry, timing/ETA definitions and diagnostic events. Measurements cover this loaded session; a checkpoint’s previous elapsed time is not reconstructed.
Retry after evaluation
Retry the final held-out test without another training update or source-file reconfiguration. Reuses a matching retained checkpoint; prepares a new snapshot only if missing or stale. An unusable GPU requires downloading the retained checkpoint and restoring it in a healthy session. Disk saving is not verified.
Save after report
Download the automatic before/after report with model, corpus, context and evaluation identity. A browser download request is not confirmation of a saved disk file.
Start / continue
Validate selected files/settings, run any needed before tests, then train or resume. Completed checkpoints skip all optimizer updates and run only a pending after test. Do not close another active run before verifying its checkpoint save.
Pause / cancel
Request a pause at the next safely committed update, then save a checkpoint. During evaluation it cancels that test. The current GPU update is not partially counted as training progress.
Reset loaded state
Release GPU state and discard unsaved in-memory progress. Save and verify a checkpoint first. This does not overwrite original files; the next loaded run starts fresh timing counters.
Save checkpoint
Download a resumable snapshot with factor masters, optimizer state, exact progress and identity checks. Keep it alongside the matching original model and corpus/plan. Verify it exists on disk before closing the tab.
Export packed GGUF
Download recovered packed factor weights. Packing rounds scales to FP16, so the export is not identical to the evaluated FP32 masters and needs its own evaluation before a packed-model quality claim.
Activity log
Ready. No recovery has started.

What & why: Run length
Continue to the remaining training budget, or pause after 1, 25 or 100 additional committed updates for a bounded check. Partial runs save a checkpoint without claiming a final after score. A pause during the final update still completes the budget and runs the after test.
